Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem (UTI/cystitis):
- Patient Goal(s): Achieve symptom resolution; prevent recurrence  
- Clinical Goal(s): Eradicate urinary infection; monitor for complications or recurrence  
- Actions (Patient): Obtain and start prescribed antibiotics promptly; increase fluid intake (2.5–3 liters/day); monitor temperature and symptoms; seek further care if symptoms worsen or recur  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Prescribe 3-day antibiotic course avoiding clindamycin; provide advice regarding hydration and adjunct measures (cranberry juice, urine acidity sachets); instruct patient on symptoms warranting re-evaluation; coordinate with pharmacy for prescription fulfilment  

Secondary Problem (possible urolithiasis):
- Patient Goal(s): Prevent potential development or complications if applicable  
- Clinical Goal(s): Monitor symptom progression; rule out stone presence if symptoms persist or worsen  
- Actions (Patient): Report any worsening pain, new symptoms such as flank pain, or difficulty urinating  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Reassess if symptoms persist post-treatment; consider imaging to exclude stones if clinically indicated  

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes  
- Topics Covered: Recognition of symptom worsening (increasing pain, fever, back pain, difficulty urinating); importance of hydration; antibiotic adherence; when to seek urgent medical review  
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increased or persistent pain, onset of fever, lower back or flank pain, inability to void urine, recurrent hematuria  
- Coping Strategies: Emphasis on fluid intake, symptomatic monitoring, and prompt medical contact if symptoms escalate

- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded (physical health plan focus)  
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: None documented

- Review Date: Suggested review if no improvement after antibiotic course or earlier if symptoms worsen; exact date not documented  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Urinary tract infection (cystitis) — High likelihood  
  Justification: Classic presentation of dysuria, hematuria, lower abdominal pain, unpleasant urine odor without systemic symptoms.
- Urolithiasis (bladder or urethral stones) — Medium likelihood  
  Justification: Hematuria and pain present, but absence of flank pain and sudden colic pain reduces likelihood.
- Urethritis (possibly STI-related) — Medium likelihood  
  Justification: Dysuria and hematuria noted; absence of discharge or sexual risk factors lowers probability.
